Descrivi il nodulo in B-mode e il suo co: Describe the nodule on B-mode and its behavior after contrast in the different phases; what is the CEUS LI-RADS category?
In un fegato a rischio ogni nodulo solid:
In an at-risk liver every solid nodule ≥ 1 cm must be characterized with contrast. On CEUS (CEUS LI-RADS v2017) typical hepatocellular carcinoma shows diffuse, non-rim arterial hyperenhancement (APHE), followed by late (after 60 seconds) and mild washout: with size ≥ 10 mm it is LR-5. Early washout (before 60 seconds) or marked washout within 2 minutes, or rim APHE, indicate LR-M (cholangiocarcinoma, metastasis, atypical hepatocellular carcinoma) and require biopsy.
In this case the nodule is almost invisible on B-mode: CEUS makes it evident, first as a brighter area in the arterial phase and then as a darker area in the late phases. The ultrasound contrast agent (microbubbles) stays within the vessels: for this reason the late, mild washout of hepatocellular carcinoma is clearly seen and should not be confused with the early and marked washout of non-hepatocellular lesions.
Teaching limitation: the images are still and the frames between about 30 seconds and 2:52 are missing, so the exact onset of washout is not documented; at 2:52 the nodule is only moderately darker, as expected for late, mild washout. In practice the LR-5 category is assigned by watching the entire sequence live or the recorded cine loop.
